visuals.title: Where the excess cortisol comes from
visuals.text: Pituitary (Cushing's disease), lung tumours making ectopic ACTH, or the adrenal glands above the kidneys.

visuals.title: What excess cortisol does
nodes: Protein catabolism: wasting, thin skin, striae

visuals.title: Why potassium falls
nodes: Kidney retains Na, loses K and H+

visuals.title: Bones and immunity
visuals.text: Osteoblasts suppressed and resorption raised: osteoporosis. Immune function impaired: infections, poor healing.

glossary.Corticosteroid: A steroid hormone or drug that acts like cortisol or aldosterone.
glossary.Adrenal carcinoma: A rare cancer of the adrenal cortex that can secrete cortisol.
glossary.Pituitary tumour: A growth of the pituitary gland at the base of the brain; usually benign.
glossary.Pituitary adenoma: A benign tumour of the pituitary gland.
glossary.Adrenal hyperplasia: Enlargement of the adrenal glands with overproduction of hormones.
glossary.Purple striae: Wide purple stretch marks on the abdomen, thighs or arms from thin, fragile skin.
glossary.Proximal muscle weakness: Weakness of the shoulder and hip muscles, making it hard to stand from sitting.
glossary.Diurnal cortisol variation: The normal daily rhythm of cortisol, highest in the morning and lowest at midnight.
glossary.Metabolic alkalosis: A raised blood pH from too much bicarbonate or loss of acid.
glossary.Bilateral adrenalectomy: Surgical removal of both adrenal glands.
glossary.Visual field defects: Loss of parts of the visual field, often from a pituitary mass pressing on the optic chiasm.
glossary.Plasma ACTH: Blood level of ACTH, used to tell ACTH-dependent from ACTH-independent causes.
glossary.Phenytoin: Anti-epileptic drug that induces liver enzymes and speeds dexamethasone breakdown.
glossary.Carbamazepine: Anti-epileptic drug that induces liver enzymes and speeds dexamethasone breakdown.
glossary.Rifampicin: Antibiotic for TB that strongly induces liver enzymes.
glossary.Pituitary MRI: Magnetic resonance scan of the pituitary to find an ACTH-secreting adenoma.
glossary.Adrenal CT: Computed tomography of the adrenal glands to look for an adenoma or carcinoma.
glossary.Wean: Reduce a drug dose gradually rather than stopping it suddenly.
glossary.Steroid synthesis inhibitor: Drug that blocks enzymes making cortisol in the adrenal glands.
glossary.Rheumatoid arthritis: Autoimmune inflammatory joint disease often treated with steroids.
glossary.Osteoporosis: Thin, fragile bones that break easily.
glossary.Insulin resistance: Body tissues respond poorly to insulin, so blood glucose rises.
glossary.Fat redistribution: Movement of body fat to the trunk, face and back of neck.
glossary.Immune function: The body's ability to fight infection.
glossary.Prolonged exposure: Being exposed to something over a long time.
glossary.Ectopic ACTH syndrome: Cushing's caused by a tumour outside the pituitary, often lung, that makes ACTH.
glossary.Pituitary: Small gland under the brain that releases ACTH and other control hormones.
glossary.Suppressed: Pushed down; in these tests a normal fall in cortisol or ACTH after dexamethasone.
